title: Type-accent table
description: The shape of the package's type-accent table, type-accents.json: which brand accent marks each resource_type term, keyed by the term's ID, with the slug that ID is expected to carry. It is data both sides read at build time, not a payload either sends: the front end imports it, and the plugin's build copies it into build/, where the related-resources block reads it. A type the table does not know, or whose ID now carries a different slug, gets the neutral mark on both sides. That no two rows share an ID, a slug or an accent is checked by the package's test, since a schema cannot say it.

types.description: One row per resource type that has an accent, in any order. A type with no row gets the neutral mark.

accent.description: One of the five brand accents, each a --rh-mark-* token in tokens.css and a value of the data-accent attribute card-labels.css paints the type mark from. The neutral mark is never written here: it is what a type without a row gets.

id.description: The resource_type term's ID, the same on the hosted CMS, the local wp-env and the mock CMS's seed.

slug.description: The slug the term with that ID is expected to carry, in WordPress's stored form. A term whose slug differs gets the neutral mark, so a stale row never colours the wrong type.

accent.description: The accent that marks the type.
